flashcards.back: The divine and the demonic. The divine was described; now Krishna describes the demonic.
Fearlessness, purity, nonviolence, truthfulness, compassion, forgiveness, contentment, and freedom from pride and malice.

flashcards.front: Where do the two natures lead?
flashcards.back: Divine qualities lead to liberation; demonic ones to bondage.
Hypocrisy, arrogance, pride, anger, harshness and ignorance.
That the world has no God, no moral order and no purpose beyond pleasure.
To insatiable desire, exploitation and cruelty, and to lower births: suffering is the destiny of the ignorant.
Lust, anger and greed lead to bondage. Learn to give up these three.
One freed from them does what is good for the soul and reaches the supreme abode.
Let scripture be your authority on what to do and not do, and do your duty by it.
One who ignores scripture and follows only personal desire reaches neither perfection, happiness nor the goal.

quiz.text: How many types of human beings does 16.6 name?
What do the demonic believe about the world?

options.C: It has no God or moral order

quiz.why: That view breeds endless desire and cruelty.

quiz.text: What are the three gates to hell (16.21)?
What should be the authority for right action (16.24)?
quiz.why: Do your duty following the scripture.

quiz.text: One who ignores scripture and follows desire attains:

slides.title: Divine and demonic qualities
bullets: Two natures, three gates, one guide

slides.title: Two kinds of people
bullets: Fearlessness, purity, truth, compassion lead to freedom

slides.title: The demonic view
bullets: No God, no moral order, only pleasure

slides.title: Three gates to hell
